title: Travel Emergency Plan: Lost Passport, Stolen Phone, Medical
expectedOutcome:
**Trip: India — US passport — solo — 14 days — World Nomads policy**

**Before you leave (do today, 10 min):**
- Photocopy passport bio page + visa, leave one with family, carry one in your backpack.
- Scan passport + insurance card + cards-in-wallet to a private cloud folder.
- Write down: insurance 24/7 hotline, family emergency contact, your blood type + allergies on a card in your wallet.
- Add embassy + local police number to phone contacts AND to a paper card in wallet.
- Tell your bank the dates so cards don't get blocked.

---

**1. Lost or stolen passport**

*First 30 min:*
1. File a police report at the nearest station (need this for the embassy). Get a stamped copy.
2. Call US Embassy New Delhi: +91-11-2419-8000 (24h ACS line: +91-11-2419-8001).
3. Book the earliest emergency appointment via travel.state.gov.

*Need ready:* photocopy of bio page, passport-sized photo (or get one at any Indian photo studio for ~₹100), proof of US citizenship.

*Cost:* Emergency passport ~$165. World Nomads usually reimburses with police report.

*Call home:* family + insurance — they may overnight documents.

---

**2. Phone stolen**

*First 30 min:*
1. From a friend's/cafe's phone or laptop: log in to Google/Apple ID → 'Find My' → **erase device + sign out** of everything. (Wait 10 min in case it's just misplaced.)
2. Call US bank fraud lines (you saved them on paper, right?). Freeze cards.
3. Police report (same station as above — needed for insurance).
4. Replacement SIM at any Airtel/Jio shop with your passport.

*Cost:* SIM swap ₹200–500. Cheap Android replacement ₹5000+. Insurance covers up to claim limit.

---

**3. Medical emergency**

*First 30 min:*
1. Ambulance: **102** (India national). For private: Apollo Hospital emergency lines vary by city.
2. Call World Nomads emergency: +1-410-453-6330 (collect-call OK) BEFORE major procedures if possible — pre-authorization affects coverage.
3. Pay first, claim later (Indian hospitals usually require deposit). Keep every receipt, every prescription, every diagnosis sheet.

*Costs:* Private hospital deposit ₹25,000–₹1,00,000 typical. Insurance covers; you may pay upfront.

---

**Print this. Fold it. Put it in your backpack and your luggage.**
tips: Test 'Find My iPhone' from a laptop *before* you leave — most people only learn the flow when they actually lose the phone.

title: Sunday Meal Prep Plan That Doesn't Get Old by Thursday
expectedOutcome:
**Lunch + dinner, 5 weekdays, 2 adults, no restrictions, maintenance, intermediate, oven+stove+instant pot, $90/week, love Mediterranean+Thai, hate olives**

**Strategy:** Cook 4 mix-and-match 'components' (1 grain, 2 proteins, 1 sauce + roasted veg). Each day you assemble a different bowl. Burnout comes from identical meals, not identical ingredients — same chicken + 4 different sauces = 4 different meals.

**Shopping list**
- *Produce:* sweet potatoes (3), broccoli (1 head), red onions (2), cherry tomatoes (1 pint), lemons (3), cilantro, mint, garlic, ginger
- *Proteins:* chicken thighs boneless (1.5 lbs), shrimp frozen (1 lb), eggs (12), chickpeas canned (2)
- *Pantry:* basmati rice (2 cups dry), olive oil, fish sauce, soy sauce, peanut butter, tahini
- *Dairy:* Greek yogurt (large), feta

**Sunday cook order (2h 15m, ~45 min active):**
1. (0:00) Preheat oven 425°F. Cube + season sweet potatoes + broccoli + red onion → sheet pan #1.
2. (0:05) Marinate chicken in lemon-garlic-olive oil; sheet pan #2.
3. (0:15) Both sheet pans go in oven (timer 25 min).
4. (0:18) Instant Pot: rinse rice + 2.5 cups water, pressure 4 min + 10 min natural release.
5. (0:25) Whisk Thai peanut sauce + lemon-tahini sauce in 2 jars.
6. (0:40) Pans out, rest. Cook shrimp 4 min on stove with garlic + lemon.
7. (1:00) Cool, then portion components into containers (don't combine).

**Weekday combos:**
- *Mon lunch:* rice + chicken + roasted veg + tahini sauce + feta
- *Mon dinner:* rice + shrimp + roasted veg + peanut sauce + mint
- *Tue lunch:* chickpea + tomato + cucumber salad + tahini + feta (no reheating)
- *Tue dinner:* chicken stir-fry kit (toss with peanut sauce + sesame + scallion fresh)
- *Wed:* breakfast-for-dinner — soft scramble + roasted veg + sriracha
- *Thu:* shrimp + rice + lemon-cilantro yogurt + cucumber
- *Fri:* clean-out bowl — everything left + fresh herbs + a fried egg on top

**Day 5 freshness fix:** keep 1 fresh herb bunch + 1 lemon + 1 cucumber untouched until Thursday night. Acid + herbs revive any prep.

**Cost:** ~$85. **Weeknight active time:** 5–8 min (reheat + assemble).
tips: Store sauces separately. Sauce-on-rice from Sunday tastes 'old' by Wednesday. Sauce poured fresh on Wednesday tastes new.

title: Recipe Substitution Without Ruining the Dish
expectedOutcome:
**Recipe:** Classic chocolate chip cookies (Toll House-style)
**Missing:** baking soda (have baking powder, salt, everything else)

**Best substitute:** Use 3× the amount of baking powder. If the recipe calls for 1 tsp baking soda → use 3 tsp baking powder.

**What changes:**
- *Spread:* less. Baking soda forces cookies to spread; baking powder lifts them. Expect cakier, taller cookies.
- *Color:* slightly paler. Baking soda raises pH which deepens browning. You'll lose 10-20% of that golden edge.
- *Texture:* softer/puffier center, less chewy.
- *Flavor:* very subtle metallic note from extra baking powder; usually masked by chocolate.

**2nd-best:** Self-rising flour swap. Replace your AP flour 1:1 with self-rising and omit both the salt and the leavener entirely. Same caveat: cakier.

**Skip it entirely?** No — without leavening you'll get dense hockey pucks. Even old beer or sparkling water mixed into the dough is better than nothing.

**Don't substitute with:**
- Yeast (wrong leavener, wrong timeline).
- Cream of tartar alone (needs the base part of baking soda).
- 'Just leave it out' — bakers tell you that for muffins, not Toll House cookies.
tips: Snap a picture of the result and ask the model 'why did this turn out [puffier/flatter/paler] than I wanted?' — debugging baking after the fact is half the value.

title: 12-Week Beginner Workout Plan You'll Actually Finish
expectedOutcome:
**Profile:** 34F, 5'5", 175 lbs, 1h walking/week, goal: strength + sleep, 3 days/week, 45 min, dumbbells (8 + 15 lbs) + bench, no knee/back issues.

**Phase 1 (Weeks 1-4) — Get the habit**
*What to expect:* Soreness peaks in week 1-2, drops by week 3. If you finish week 1 cursing me, plan is right.

**Week 1 (sample):**
- *Mon — Full body A (40 min):*
  - Goblet squat (15 lb DB): 3×8, RIR 4
  - DB Romanian deadlift: 3×8, RIR 4
  - Incline DB press (15 lb): 3×8, RIR 4
  - One-arm DB row: 3×8/side, RIR 4
  - Plank: 3×20 sec
- *Wed — Cardio (30 min):* brisk walk + 2 × 1-min slightly-uphill (zone 2)
- *Fri — Full body B (40 min):*
  - DB step-up: 3×8/side, RIR 4
  - DB sumo deadlift: 3×8, RIR 4
  - DB shoulder press seated: 3×8, RIR 4
  - DB pullover: 3×8, RIR 4
  - Side plank: 3×15 sec/side
- *Saturday or Sunday — 10-min mobility:* cat-cow, hip openers, thoracic rotations

**Self-check end of week:** sleep score? morning energy?

**Phase 2 (Weeks 5-8) — Build**
Same template, add 1 rep/set or 5 lb where RIR ≥ 3 in week 4. Week 8 = deload (back to week 5 volume).

**Phase 3 (Weeks 9-12) — Test**
Move to 4×6 with RIR 2. Week 12 is a 'retest': same exercises as Week 1, same weight — see how the reps feel. That's your real progress.

*What to expect:* week 6 hits the wall (motivation dip — normal). Week 10 you'll notice the bag of groceries is lighter.

**Missed-day rule:** if you miss 2 days in a row, repeat the prior week — don't 'catch up' with extra volume. Volume catch-up = injury.
tips: Track in a 1-line journal: 'Mon — squat 15 × 8, RIR 4, knee fine, slept 7h.' That's the whole log. Anything more detailed gets abandoned by week 4.

title: 30-Minute Workout Plan for Insanely Busy Weeks
expectedOutcome:
**Intermediate, dumbbells + bench, hate burpees, no injuries**

**Session A — Lower + push (30 min)**
*Warmup (5 min):* 1 min march-in-place, 10 squats, 10 hip-circles each direction, 10 reach-overheads, 5 pushups.

*Circuit — 4 rounds, 35s work / 25s rest:*
1. Goblet squat — cue: drive knees out, chest up. *Regression:* bodyweight squat to chair. *Progression:* 1.5 reps.
2. DB bench or floor press — cue: shoulder blades pinned. *Regression:* pushup. *Progression:* slow 4-sec eccentric.
3. DB Romanian deadlift — cue: hinge from hips, weights stay close to legs. *Regression:* lighter DB. *Progression:* single-leg.
4. Plank — cue: ribs down, glutes squeezed.

*Cooldown (3 min):* couch stretch each leg + child's pose.

**Session B — Pull + core (30 min)**
*Warmup:* same.
*Circuit:*
1. One-arm DB row
2. DB curl + shoulder press combo
3. DB suitcase carry (40 sec each side)
4. Dead bug

**Session C — Conditioning (30 min)**
*Warmup:* same.
*Circuit — 6 rounds, 40s work / 20s rest:*
1. Kettlebell-style DB swing (or bodyweight: jump squat)
2. Push press
3. Reverse lunge alternating
4. Mountain climber slow

**Bare-minimum 15-min day:** 3 rounds — goblet squat × 12, row × 10/side, plank 30 sec. That's it.

**Rotation:** Week 1-3: A/B/C. Week 4-6: switch DB press → DB pullover, RDL → single-leg RDL. Week 7-9: add 1 round each session. Week 10: deload (3 rounds of A only). Repeat.
tips: Pick the session order *the night before*. Decision fatigue at 6:30am kills more workouts than soreness does.

title: Couch-to-5K Running Plan Tailored to Your Real Schedule
expectedOutcome:
**Profile: 32M, intermediate baseline (can run 5 min slow), 3 days/week, road in 50-70°F, no injuries, prior attempts died from boredom**

**Week 1 (RPE 4)**
- *Tue:* 5 min walk warmup → run 1 min / walk 2 min × 6 → 5 min walk cooldown
- *Thu:* same as Tue
- *Sat:* 5 min walk → run 2 min / walk 2 min × 5 → 5 min walk
- *Strength (Wed):* 15 squats + 10 single-leg deadlifts/side + 30s plank — 3 rounds.

**Week 2 (RPE 4):** Run 2 / walk 2 × 6, 3×/wk
**Week 3:** Run 3 / walk 2 × 5
**Week 4:** Run 4 / walk 2 × 4
**Week 5:** Run 5 / walk 2 × 4
**Week 6:** Run 7 / walk 1 × 3
**Week 7:** Run 10 / walk 1 × 2
**Week 8:** Run 15 continuous → 20 → 25 over 3 sessions
**Week 9:** Run 30 min continuous (the 5K)

**Progression rule:** if last week's RPE > 6, repeat the week — don't push forward.

**Missed last week?** Repeat it. Always. Do not 'catch up'.

**Failure mode fixes:**
- *Shin splints:* drop to walk-only for 5-7 days, ice, replace shoes if >300mi.
- *Bored:* a podcast you only allow yourself to listen to while running. Plot device that pulls you out the door.
- *Too hard:* slower pace, never longer interval. RPE > 6 means you're running too fast.
- *Too cold:* hat + gloves + base layer beats giving up. Layer for '20°F warmer than reality'.
tips: Run slower than you think you should. If you can't say one full sentence out loud while running, slow down. Pace is the hidden killer of every C25K attempt.

title: Sleep Schedule Fix for Erratic / Late-Night Hours
expectedOutcome:
**Your data shows:** bedtimes 1:30am-3am Mon-Fri, wake 9-11am, 1-2 naps (20-90 min) in afternoons. Coffee 3-4 cups, last at 6pm. 2 alcohol drinks in last week. Phone in bed 60-90 min. No morning light — first 30 min is phone in bed.

**The 2 things wrecking you:**
1. **Variable wake time** swings of 2 hours. Your circadian clock can't pick a time zone. Bedtime drifts to follow.
2. **No morning light.** Your phone tells your brain it's still night for the first hour. Melatonin doesn't drop on schedule, so neither does the next bedtime.

Caffeine and alcohol are real but secondary. Fix the two above first.

**Days 1-3 — Anchor wake time only.** Pick *one* wake time that works for your worst weekday (say 9:30am). Use that every day, weekends included. Don't change bedtime yet — just wake.

**Days 4-6 — Add 10 min outside light within 30 min of waking.** Yes, even cloudy days. Coffee can wait until you've been outside.

**Days 7-9 — Caffeine cutoff at 1:30pm.** Based on your 6pm last-cup → 1am bedtime data, 1:30 should put you in the clear by 11pm.

**Days 10-12 — Phone out of bed.** Put it on a charger across the room. Read paperback / journal in bed if you need a wind-down activity. 30 min screen-free before lights-out.

**Days 13-14 — Anchor bedtime.** By now your sleep pressure will pull bedtime earlier on its own. Pick a target (12:30am for your schedule) and hold it within ±30 min.

**After a bad night:** do NOT nap > 20 min, do NOT sleep in. Hold the wake time. One bad night becomes one. Two compensations become two weeks.

**Not fixable for now:** if you're on-call or have a newborn, ignore everything above and just protect the morning light habit. Light > consistency > duration.
tips: Track only 3 numbers: bedtime, wake time, morning light yes/no. Five-metric sleep apps make people anxious and abandon tracking.

title: How to Build an Emergency Fund From Where You Actually Are
expectedOutcome:
**Take-home $4,800 · bare-bones $2,900 · current savings $400 · CC $3,200 @ 23% APR · salaried, 1 dependent · health insurance yes, disability no**

**Right-sized target: 4 months bare-bones = $11,600.** Salaried with one dependent and no disability insurance puts you in the middle of the range. Skip 6 months until disability is in place.

**Surplus calculation:** $4,800 take-home − $2,900 bare-bones − $300 'real life buffer' (kid stuff, gas) = **$1,600/month of true surplus**.

**Phase 1 — $1K starter (within 2 weeks).** Move $600 from this month + $0 elsewhere → done. This is what stops a $700 car repair from going on the credit card.

**Phase 2 — Kill the 23% APR CC (3 months).** Throw $1,000/mo at it. Done by end of month 4. Mathematically beats any savings rate. Keep your starter buffer at $1K while you do this — don't drain it for debt.

**Phase 3 — Build to $11,600 (7-8 months).**
- Month 5-12: $1,300/mo to emergency fund. (After CC freed up $250/mo minimum.)
- Target hit: month 12.

**Where to park it:**
- US: HYSA at Marcus, Ally, or Wealthfront cash (~4-5% APY). Same liquidity as checking, no risk.
- Or 4-week T-bills laddered if rates beat HYSA significantly.
- NOT in stocks. NOT in your 401k. NOT in a 'high yield' app paying 8%.

**Don't:**
- Keep it in checking. You will spend it.
- 'Park it' in a brokerage in S&P 500 'for higher returns'. It's not for returns.
- Use it for a planned expense (Christmas, vacation, wedding). Those are sinking funds.
- Touch it for anything except: job loss, medical, urgent car/housing repair.

**Year 2:** if income stable, push to 6 months ($17,400) and start funding disability insurance — that's the missing piece.
tips: $1K in a savings account stops more financial spirals than $11K in a brokerage. Phase 1 first, every time.

title: How to Invest Your First $1,000 (No Crypto Bro Energy)
expectedOutcome:
**US, 28, $65K income, employer 401k match yes (3%) but you only contribute 2%, no IRA, 3 months emergency fund, $0 CC debt, time horizon 10+ years, 'okay' risk**

**Stop. Before this $1K — do this first:**
- Bump your 401k contribution from 2% → 3% to grab the full employer match. That's literally free money (~$650/yr) you're leaving on the table. This is a bigger win than anything you'll do with this $1,000.

**Now the $1,000:**

**Account:** Open a Roth IRA at Fidelity, Vanguard, or Schwab. Roth = you've already paid taxes, money grows tax-free. At 28 with $65K income, Roth dominates traditional for you.

**What to buy:** Boring 3-fund portfolio or a single target-date fund.

*Option A — simplest, 1 fund:*
- 100% FXIFX (Fidelity Target 2065 Index) — auto-rebalances over 35 years, expense ratio 0.12%.

*Option B — 3-fund DIY:*
- 70% FZROX (Fidelity Total US Stock Market, 0% expense)
- 20% FZILX (Fidelity Total International, 0% expense)
- 10% FXNAX (Fidelity Total Bond, 0.025%)

**Why this isn't sexy:** these funds will look 'boring' on any forum. They will beat 80% of active investors over 20 years. Sexy is what blows up your account. Index investing wins by *not* doing the exciting thing.

**This weekend (60 min):**
1. Open Fidelity Roth IRA online (15 min).
2. Link your bank, transfer $1,000.
3. Once funds settle (1 business day), set buy order for Option A or B above.
4. Set up $200/mo auto-contribution from now on.
5. Close the app for 90 days. (Seriously. Checking it daily is the enemy.)

**Worst case:** in a 2008-style year, this $1K could be ~$600. You don't sell. You don't panic. You keep adding monthly. 10 years later it's $4-5K assuming long-term averages. Selling at $600 is the only mistake.
tips: If you can't tell yourself 'I will not sell when this drops 40%', you're not ready yet. Get to that mental place before adding more.

title: Realistic 90-Day Plan to Improve Your Credit Score
expectedOutcome:
**Score 632 FICO · limits $8K total · balances $4,800 (60% util) · 4 cards · oldest 4 years · 1 missed payment 14 months ago · 0 collections · planning mortgage in 6 months · stable income**

**What's killing your score right now:**
1. **Utilization 60%.** This is the biggest single factor here. Each $1,000 you pay down moves you 12.5 percentage points. Below 10% across all cards is the sweet spot; below 30% is the cutoff.
2. **Missed payment 14 months ago.** Less of a drag than utilization but still ~30-50 points. Time + perfect payments are the only fix.

Doing both: realistic 90-day move = +50 to +90 points.

**Weeks 1-2:**
- Pull all 3 reports at annualcreditreport.com. Dispute any errors (wrong balances, duplicate accounts, ages). Each error fix can be worth 10-30 points.
- Set autopay on all 4 cards to at-least-minimum (kills future missed payments).
- Make a payment to your highest-utilization card to drop it under 30% individually.

**Weeks 3-6:**
- Pay $1,500 toward balances — target highest-utilization cards first (not highest APR — utilization is the lever here).
- Aim: total utilization → 30%.
- Make a mid-cycle payment so the statement balance reported to the bureaus is the lower number (utilization is calculated from statement balance, not current balance — this is the #1 hack people miss).

**Weeks 7-12:**
- Pay another $1,500-2,000 → total utilization 10%.
- Verify with a fresh score pull (free via Credit Karma or your card's monitoring tool — note: VantageScore not FICO, but trend is the same).

**What WON'T help in 90 days:**
- Closing old cards (this *raises* utilization and shortens history — opposite of what you want).
- Paying off a 14-month-old missed payment again — it's already paid; just let it age.
- Asking a card issuer to remove the missed payment (goodwill letters work occasionally, not reliably; try it once, move on).

**Don't:**
- Apply for a new card 'to raise your limit'. Hard pull = -3 to -8 points + new account lowers average age. Worth it AFTER mortgage closes, not before.
- Co-sign anyone's anything.
- Touch credit-repair companies.

**At day 90, ~700 FICO:** conventional mortgage tier (3.5-5% down possible), car APR ~6-8% instead of 12%+. Real money.
tips: Pay the card down 7 days before the statement closes — that's the balance reported to bureaus. Most people pay on the due date, after it's already been reported.

title: Rent vs Buy: Real Math For Your Actual Numbers
expectedOutcome:
**City: Seattle · rent $2,800 · purchase $720K · 20% down ($144K) · 6.8% rate · property tax 0.95% · no HOA · insurance $130/mo · maint $600/mo (1%/yr) · plan to stay 7 years**

**Monthly cost of owning:**
- Mortgage P+I (30yr fixed, $576K loan at 6.8%): $3,756
- Property tax: $570
- Insurance: $130
- Maintenance: $600
- Opportunity cost on $144K down payment (assume 7% in index = $10,080/yr = $840/mo)
- **Total true monthly cost: $5,896**

**Renting cost:** $2,800/mo. Difference of $3,096/mo cheaper.

IF you rent and invest that $3,096/mo difference + the $144K at 7%: after 7 years the rent path is sitting on $483K invested.

IF you buy: 7 years of mortgage payments builds ~$108K equity. House appreciates at 3% per year (Seattle long-term avg) → $897K. Subtract selling costs (6%) = $843K. Subtract remaining mortgage ($510K) = $333K cash from sale.

**7-year net position:** Rent + invest: ~$483K. Buy: ~$333K. **Renting wins by ~$150K** at these numbers.

**Break-even:** ~13 years at current rates.

**What flips it:**
- Rate drops to 5.5% → break-even 9 years.
- Seattle appreciation jumps to 5%/yr → break-even 8 years.
- You stay 12+ years → buying wins.
- You'd actually invest the savings (most people don't — they spend it) → renting only wins if you actually invest.

**Non-financial:**
- *Buy makes sense:* you've got kids in a specific school zone, your career is locked here, you want the payment certainty of a fixed mortgage.
- *Rent makes sense:* job might relocate, you hate calling plumbers, you'd rather invest the difference, Seattle inventory might shift.

Your numbers say **rent + invest the difference** for 7 years. Reassess at year 5 if rates drop or your timeline extends.
tips: The single most-skipped cost: opportunity cost on the down payment. That $144K isn't 'free' just because it's in a house — it has a job.

title: 30-Day Moving Checklist That Doesn't Forget the Annoying Stuff
expectedOutcome:
**Move: Brooklyn → Austin · 3 weeks out · hired movers + driving car down · couple, 1 dog · current lease ends day 30 · budget $4K**

**Week 1 (T-30 to T-22)**
*Logistics:* get 3 mover quotes (long-distance varies $1.5K-$4K). Reserve preferred move date. Book hotel for 1 night midway (your dog can't do 26h in one go).
*Packing:* declutter — donate run on day 23-25 (Goodwill drop, FB Marketplace for furniture). Photograph and list 5 'maybe' items on Marketplace.
*Paperwork:* notify landlord in writing (60-day notice if your lease requires; check yours). Pull your move-in inspection photos.
*People:* tell employer + book any remote-work days you need for the move.

**Week 2 (T-21 to T-15)**
*Logistics:* confirm mover. Order packing supplies: 30 small + 20 medium + 5 large boxes, tape, markers, paper.
*Packing:* pack books, holiday decor, off-season clothes (anything you won't touch in 21 days).
*Paperwork:* USPS change-of-address (file ~10 days before move). Notify bank, credit cards, insurance, voter registration. Update DMV after move (TX requires 30 days).
*People:* find new vet in Austin, transfer dog records. School records if applicable.

**Week 3 (T-14 to T-8)**
*Logistics:* schedule internet install for day 1 in new place (Spectrum + Google Fiber both serve Austin). Cancel current internet for day after move.
*Packing:* kitchen non-essentials, bathroom non-essentials. Label boxes by ROOM, not contents.
*Paperwork:* refill prescriptions 90 days out at CVS (transfers to any branch nationwide). Update dog license. Forward voter reg.
*People:* host a 'help us empty the fridge' dinner — saves food + says goodbye.

**Week 4 (T-7 to T-1)**
*Logistics:* defrost freezer 48h before, eat down fridge. Confirm mover arrival window.
*Packing:* essentials box (1 per person): meds, charger, change of clothes, toothbrush, dog leash + food, important documents. KEEP THIS IN YOUR CAR.
*Paperwork:* take 40+ photos of every wall, floor, appliance for security deposit. Email them to yourself + landlord same day.
*People:* finalize key handover with landlord.

**Move day:** Movers arrive AM. You meet them, then drive ahead with the essentials box + dog. Photo of empty apartment before locking up.

**Day 1 new place:** unpack only the essentials box + kitchen + bedroom. Set up internet. Find the nearest dog park. Order pizza, don't try to unpack everything.

**Most-forgotten:**
1. **Security deposit walk-through photos** with timestamps.
2. **Prescription transfer** (chains do it instantly; small pharmacies need notice).
3. **Internet appointment booked AT new place** before move day, not after.
tips: The 'essentials box' rides in your car, not the truck. Movers can be late by a day. Your toothbrush and dog leash cannot.

title: Roommate Agreement That Prevents Awkward Fights Later

*Roommates: Sasha + Devon · Move-in: Sept 1 · Lease: 12 months*

**1. Money**
- Rent: $2,400/mo, split $1,200 each. Paid by Sasha to landlord by the 1st. Devon Venmos Sasha by the 28th of the prior month.
- Utilities (~$140/mo avg): split 50/50. Devon pays internet directly ($65), Sasha pays electric ($60-90 variable). Truing up quarterly.

**2. Cleaning**
- Kitchen counters + dishes: clean within 24 hours of using.
- Bathroom: rotated weekly (Sasha odd weeks, Devon even). Includes wipe-down, toilet, mirror, mop.
- Living room/floors: rotated weekly (opposite person to bathroom).
- Trash: whoever fills it takes it out. No 'I'll do it tomorrow' on overflowing bags.
- Big clean (oven, fridge, windows): once a quarter, together, 90 min.

**3. Guests**
- Overnight guests OK with 12+ hr heads-up.
- 3 nights/week max for regular partners. Beyond that, conversation about cost-share.
- 'Living here unofficially' threshold: 5+ nights/week for 3+ weeks running.

**4. Quiet hours**
- Weekdays: 10:30pm – 7am.
- Weekends: 12am – 9am.
- Headphones after 10pm — even in your own room.

**5. Food**
- Separate groceries.
- Shared staples we'll buy together: olive oil, salt/pepper, coffee, dish soap, TP, paper towels. Sasha buys odd months, Devon even.
- Anything in the fridge with your name on it is off-limits unless asked. No name = fair game by day 5.

**6. Pets**
- Devon's cat Mochi: Devon handles litter, food, vet. Mochi stays out of Sasha's room.

**7. Conflict resolution**
- Monthly 'house check-in' 15 min, first Sunday of the month, coffee. Anything bothering us comes up there before it builds.
- Anything urgent: bring it up within 48 hours, in person, not via passive-aggressive text.

- 60-day notice to roommate if you plan to leave.
- Last month's rent is paid normally, not subtracted from the security deposit.
- Security deposit refund: split based on lease landlord's return + any deductions allocated by whose room/damage.

*Signed:* ____________ (Sasha) · ____________ (Devon) · Date: ____
tips: Sign it on day 1, not day 60. The agreement isn't worth a thing once the first conflict has already happened.

title: Diagnose Why Your Plant Is Dying (and Save It)
expectedOutcome:
**Plant:** Monstera deliciosa, 1.5 years owned. Yellow leaves (3 lower leaves in last 10 days), brown spots developing on the yellow ones, soil feels wet 4 days after watering. Currently 5 ft from south-facing window with sheer curtain. Watering ~1x/week, 1 cup. Pot has drainage hole. Regular potting mix. Last fertilized 6 months ago. No recent moves.

**Most-likely diagnosis: overwatering / early root rot.**

Monstera should dry out the top 2 inches between waterings. Yours stays wet for 4+ days, which is the classic signature. Yellow-to-brown lower leaves + wet soil is the textbook sequence.

**Alternate worth checking:** nutrient deficiency from 6 months without fertilizer. Less likely as primary because the soil-wetness clue points harder at watering.

**Triage (today):**
1. Skip watering until top 2 inches are bone-dry. Stick your finger in — if you feel any moisture, wait.
2. Tip the pot, slide the plant out (don't yank). Look at the roots: healthy = white/cream and firm. Rot = brown/black, mushy, or smells.
3. If any root rot: trim brown/mushy roots with clean scissors. Don't repot wet — let the root ball air-dry on newspaper for 4 hours.
4. Repot in fresh, dry potting mix with extra perlite (50/50). The drainage hole stays. Don't water for 5-7 days after repot.

**Recovery plan (4 weeks):**
- Water only when top 2 inches feel dry. For your Monstera in that light, that's typically every 10-14 days, not 7.
- Move 2-3 ft closer to the window — sheer curtain stays, but light is the engine that lets the soil dry.
- Fertilize at 1/2 strength once new growth shows. Skip until then.
- Don't mist excessively. Don't move it around looking for the 'perfect' spot — once a week is the max change rate.

**Give up if:** by week 2, you see new mushy growth, the main stem is soft to the touch, or you smell rot. At that point, propagate any healthy aerial root cuttings in water and let the parent go.
tips: Take a photo of the plant today + every Sunday. Pattern over 3 weeks tells you more than any single symptom.

title: New Dog: First 30 Days Plan (Survive + Bond)
expectedOutcome:
**Dog:** 2yr female lab mix, ~50 lbs, just adopted from city shelter, unknown history, scared of men. Household: couple, no kids, no other pets. WFH 4 days / 1 office day. Apartment with elevator. New owners.

**Week 1 — Decompression**
*The 3-3-3 rule:* 3 days to settle, 3 weeks to learn the routine, 3 months to fully bond.

First week is about LOWERING the stress hormone load, nothing else. Don't introduce her to your friends. Don't take her to the dog park. Don't even bring her to your favorite cafe.

*Do:*
- Set up a quiet corner with bed, water, and the crate (door open). Let her choose where to sleep.
- 2 short, quiet walks a day. Same block. Predictability is everything.
- Hand-feed kibble from a flat palm for 5 min twice a day. Builds trust faster than any toy.
- Speak in a lower, slower voice when your partner (male) is around her. Let him toss treats without making eye contact for the first week.

*Don't:*
- Force pets. Let her come to you.
- Bath her. (Stress + new place + soap = trauma.)
- Have anyone over.

**Week 2 — Routine**
- Feed at same 2 times. Walk at same 3 times.
- Crate training: 5 min alone in apartment day 1, 10 min day 3, 20 min day 5, 45 min day 7. Reward with a stuffed Kong before each absence.
- Start sleeping in bedroom (crate or bed) — same room reduces separation anxiety long-term.
- One vet visit booked for routine check + heartworm test.

**Week 3 — Training**
- 'Find it' game: scatter 5-10 kibbles, say 'find it'. 5 min twice a day. Builds confidence + bond.
- Name + look-at-me: treat every time she looks at you when you say her name.
- Sit on a cue, with a hand signal.
- Recall: only inside or on a long line. Reward like she just won a marathon.

**Week 4 — Socialization (carefully)**
- 1 quiet new place (a different park, not the dog park). 15 min.
- Vet visit follow-up if any concerns.
- First time meeting another dog: only if both are calm, on-leash, parallel walk, never face-to-face.
- Skip the dog park for at least 2 more months. Most fights happen there.

**5 biggest mistakes:**
1. Doing 'too much, too soon' — friends over, hikes, dog parks in week 1.
2. Free-feeding (food out all day) → ruins motivation for training.
3. Skipping the crate because 'she seems sad' → crate is the safest tool you have.
4. Punishing fear (scolding her for hiding from your partner) → makes fear worse.
5. Calling a trainer too late — wait until week 6+ to evaluate behaviors, but if there's a bite by week 2, get help immediately.

**Trainer or DIY?**
- DIY: routines, basic cues, decompression.
- Trainer (force-free, positive reinforcement only): if you see fear-biting, severe resource guarding, or you simply don't know where to start. Book by week 3.

**House rules card:**
- Wait by the door, let me approach. No reaching toward my face.
- No food from the table or hand-feeding without permission.
- Don't pet me while I'm eating or sleeping.
- If I retreat to my corner/crate, please leave me alone.
tips: Resist the urge to take her to the dog park 'to socialize'. Most dog-park 'socialization' creates the reactive dogs you see at the next park.

title: Car-Buying Script: Walk Away With a Real Deal
expectedOutcome:
**Target:** 2023 Toyota RAV4 LE, used CPO. KBB private party + dealer comps say $26K is fair, $27.5K is the ceiling. Pre-approved at 6.2% from credit union. No trade-in.

**Opener (calm, direct):**
"Hi, I'm Devon. I'm here to look at the 2023 RAV4 LE on the lot. I'm pre-approved at 6.2% from my credit union and I'm paying cash for any down. I'm not trading anything in. I'll need an out-the-door price before I commit — happy to test drive first."

**The 4 numbers — track each separately, never together:**
1. **Out-the-door (OTD) price** — vehicle + tax + title + actual government fees. NOT dealer-doc fees (those are negotiable, often $399-$999 padding).
2. **Trade-in value** (n/a for you, but for others: get a written quote from CarMax or Carvana first — that's your floor).
3. **Financing rate** — your pre-approval number. Let the dealer try to beat it. If they can't, you ignore everything they say about financing.
4. **Monthly payment** — *do not negotiate on monthly payment*. That's the dealer's favorite trap because they extend the term to make the payment lower and the total cost higher. Negotiate on OTD only.

**Scripts:**

*'Let me get my manager':* "Sure, take your time. I'll wait 10 minutes — if the manager isn't free by then I'll come back tomorrow." (Time pressure is *theirs*, not yours.)

*'But it includes paint protection / fabric protection / nitrogen tires':* "Please remove those from the contract. I don't want them. If they're not removable, that tells me the OTD price isn't fixed yet."

*'We can lower your monthly payment by extending the term':* "Thanks, but I'm focused on out-the-door price, not monthly. I'll handle financing separately."

*'GAP coverage is highly recommended':* "Got it. I'll consider GAP — but only through my credit union, where it's usually 1/3 the price. Please remove it from this contract."

**Walk-away red lines:**
- OTD comes back > $28K.
- Dealer refuses to remove an add-on you didn't ask for.
- Dealer 'has to add' a mandatory fee that isn't government tax/title.
- The car has been on the lot < 7 days and they won't budge — they have buyers; come back in 2 weeks.

**Before signing, cross-check:**
- Out-the-door price matches the verbal agreement to the dollar.
- No 'paint protection,' 'theft etching,' 'nitrogen,' 'tire-and-wheel' charges unless you explicitly chose them.
- Financing line: rate matches your pre-approval (or dealer's beat). Term is what you agreed to.
- Trade-in value (if any) matches written quote.
- VIN on the contract matches the car you test-drove.

If anything is off, stop. Ask them to fix the printed contract. Don't initial a 'we'll fix it later' line.
tips: Walk out at least once. The single best price drop in car buying happens between when you leave the showroom and the salesperson's first follow-up call.
